bookings.title: Looking Back to Move Forward: Security Information Sharing and Software/Host Attestation Throughout the IETF
bookings.description:
Security information sharing, automation of countermeasures, software information flow discovery, vulnerability detection, attestation, and communication of software provenance have been discussed across numerous IETF Working Groups and Independent RFCs. Internet-enabled systems continue to evolve, and some topics may benefit from renewed attention in the IETF.
The IETF community includes participants with deep historical knowledge as well as newcomers with fresh perspectives, making historical context valuable.
In the side meeting, participants will survey existing RFCs, expired I/Ds, and closed/active WGs (e.g., SACM, DOTS, I2NSF, RFC 9116, RFC 9472, SCITT, SPICE, RATS) to identify worthwhile challenges for modern systems among remaining open issues. By sharing insights from past discussions, we hope to map problems already addressed.
If you are interested in presenting, please contact me with title/abstract & expected time by the end of the Hackathon session.

bookings.title: Interconnection and Discovery of AI Agents on the Internet
bookings.description:
This side meeting proposes an open technical discussion on architectural and protocol considerations for enabling interoperable interconnection and discovery of AI agents on the Internet.
As AI agents increasingly perform autonomous service invocation, coordination, and cross-domain collaboration, new requirements emerge around identity, service discovery, capability advertisement, interoperability, and trust. The session will explore how existing Internet architecture and IETF protocols can support AI agent onboarding and interaction, and whether new use cases or protocol extensions may need to be considered.
The discussion plans to focus on identity, service discovery, cross-domain discovery and interoperability, as well as security and trust. The objective is to share practices and ideas, gauge community interest, and explore potential next steps. Participation from protocol designers, operators, implementers, and researchers is welcome.
Organizers: Jiankang Yao & Qiong Sun

bookings.title: Agentic AI Security and Trust status and strategy at ITU-T SG17
bookings.description:

2) ensure there is no duplication of work
3) set expectations on where SG17 would like to seek collaboration with IETF 
4) discuss next steps and potential practical approaches

bookings.title: Interface to In-Network Computing Functions (I2ICF)
bookings.description:
The Interface to In-Network Computing Functions (I2ICF) group aims to define interfaces and protocols for provisioning In-Network Computing Functions (ICFs) like Application Functions (AFs) and Computing Functions (CFs) for the requested services in the aforementioned use cases. Agentic AI can be used for accommodate the intelligent services among AI agents.

In-Network Computing (INC) or Computing in the Network (COIN) is a promising technology to help solve these problems. It could help reduce the data volume and improve the Quality of Service (QoS) by offloading some AFs or CFs into In-Network Computing Functions (ICFs) such as Programmable Network Devices (PNDs).

Also, Intent-Based Networking (IBN) can compose user services autonomously and construct a combination of ICFs into a target network for service provisioning and QoS assurance. The I2ICF group will present several drafts related to I2ICF and discuss its charter and milestone to prepare for a WG-forming BoF in the IETF 126

bookings.title: AI Ecosystem and Discovery
bookings.description:
As AI agents and distributed AI systems evolve, discovery—how agents find tasks, services, capabilities, and other agents—becomes a key challenge. This side meeting brings together participants interested in agent protocols and discovery mechanisms to explore how discovery fits into the broader AI ecosystem. The goal is to discuss whether discovery should be treated as a general capability across AI systems, complementing agent-specific protocols.Presentations:
1. AI Ecosystem and Discovery in AI Networks: Separation of General Discovery and Agent Protocols 2. Task Discovery Framework: An Agent-Initiated Discovery Approach 3. Agent Registration and Discovery Protocol (ARDP) 4. Use Cases for DNS for Agentic AI Discovery 5. AI Agent Protocols for Multi-modality.
Materials will be made available on our side meeting github at:
https://github.com/DA-ITN/draft-mamwp-ai-network-task-discovery. Repository contains materials related to task discovery draft. Co-organizer: Arashmid Akhavain

bookings.title: Confidential AI
bookings.description: Remote attestation plays a central role in confidential computing. However, there are several research questions on real-world scenarios, such as confidential AI, which are out of scope of the RATS, TLS, and SEAT WG charters. In this side meeting, we aim to discuss those open research questions and collect ideas on which one of those can be solved in the IRTF/IETF. Since all confidential computing solutions use TLS protocol, we aim to use the attested TLS protocol work from SEAT as the basis of this discussion. We believe the research work does not fall within the charter of existing IRTF RGs or IETF WGs. So we would like to discuss on how to bring this work to the IRTF/IETF. We very much welcome presentations by attendees on open research topics related to attestation in confidential computing. If you are interested in presenting, please contact me with title and expected time.

bookings.title: Discussion on use case and requirements of Hybrid function chain
bookings.description:
Organizers: Chuanyang Miao [miao.chuanyang@zte.com.cn], Xinxin Yi [yixx3@chinaunicom.cn].
Summary: In cloud-native environments and service mesh scenarios, service chains offer a highly flexible approach to application implementation. However, existing service-layer chaining mechanisms rely solely on L7 (application layer) requirements and lack coordination with L3 (network layer) quality, resulting in deficiencies in end-to-end service quality across the entire runtime. This side meeting is proposed to discuss the use cases, requirements, and any potential standardization work for a hybrid function/service chain that harmonizes service requirements with both network and computing resources.

bookings.description:

bookings.title: multicast for AI networks
bookings.description: The exponential growth of LLM parameters and training data is driving GPU clusters toward million-card scale. Global players are planning such deployments, yet power, space, and site constraints make single-data-center aggregation infeasible. Interconnecting distributed intelligent computing centers for joint training or inference has thus become a major industry trend. Meanwhile, Mixture of Experts (MoE) architectures are being introduced to reduce training costs while maintaining high performance. These emerging scenarios require efficient data synchronization across geo-distributed data centers and GPU modules, involving massive point-to-multipoint transmissions—typical multicast use cases with significantly higher requirements. Applications such as MoE token distribution and model replication require multicast with high dynamics and high reliability. This meeting aims to explore technical challenges and potential solutions for multicast in AI computing networks.

bookings.title: DICE – DNS-based Intelligence and Computing Environments
bookings.description:
DNS-based Service Discovery (DNS-SD, RFC 6763) is a mature and widely deployed mechanism for discovering services across local and wide-area networks. However, emerging network paradigms—specifically Computing-Aware Traffic Steering (CATS) and the Internet of Agents (IoA)—introduce highly dynamic and context-rich requirements that challenge traditional discovery models.

In CATS architectures, optimal routing and steering decisions require visibility into both network status and dynamic computing resource availability. Similarly, the emerging Internet of Agents requires autonomous, AI-driven entities to dynamically discover, verify, and establish communications with peer agents based on specific capabilities, trust boundaries, and real-time context.

This side meeting aims to explore the applicability, limitations, and potential extensions of DNS and DNS-SD in these advanced scenarios.

bookings.title: AI Agent Policy-aware Network
bookings.description:
MPLS/SRv6 have been widely deployed in backbone networks, providing differentiated services for traditional applications. However, the rapid development of generative AI and multi-Agent systems imposes unprecedented policy-aware service requirements on networks, including ultra-low latency, high availability, on-demand scheduling, and fine-grained traffic steering. The key challenge is how to utilize existing network advantages to perceive diverse policies for AI Agent interactions and support efficient deployment and collaboration.
To address this gap, the network needs to evolve into an intelligent policy-aware service system for AI Agents. This meeting aims to discuss the scenarios, requirements, technical challenges, and deployment cases of the AI Agent Policy-Aware Network. And related technologies such as APN, ARN and NSH will also be further explored.
Organizers: Xiaoqiu Zhang & Nan Geng

bookings.title: Next-Generation Inter-Domain Routing Architecture and Protocols  (IDRNG)
bookings.description:
The IDRNG side meeting provides an open forum for researchers, operators, and protocol designers to discuss the evolution of inter-domain routing architectures and protocols in the AI era. It serves as a platform for exchanging ideas on architectural design, protocol development, security, manageability, and operational considerations for next-generation routing.

Key topics include AI-driven routing control and optimization, routing security and assurance mechanisms, and emerging requirements driven by AI workloads, including compute–network co-scheduling, latency-sensitive traffic, and energy-aware constraints. The meeting also explores multi-agent and agentic routing models across administrative domains, supports shared methodologies and experimental evaluation, and fosters collaboration on research outputs and IRTF/IETF documents.

The side meeting is open to all participants and follows IETF/IRTF principles of open participation, technical merit, and consensus-based discussion.

bookings.title: DMSC(Dynamic Multi-agent Secured Collaboration)
bookings.description:
With the rapid emergence of diverse AI agents—including host agents, device agents, network agents, and application agents—a critical challenge is to enable dynamic collaboration among these agents to perform complex tasks on behalf of end-users. At the same time, there is a growing need to ensure that such collaboration is secure, scalable, and manageable operationally. Service providers face the task of designing and optimizing a comprehensive communication architecture that enables secure and efficient collaboration between heterogeneous AI agents, ensuring the following:

Distributed agent registration and identification
Discovery of suitable peer agents
Intelligent request routing and coordination
Secure inter-agent communication and trust establishment
Sustained high performance and operational visibility
To address these challenges, the DMSC side meeting will discuss the solutions for above issues and the proposed charter of future BoF/WG.

bookings.title: Transport Layer Protocols Optimization for Satellite Networks(T4SAT)
bookings.description:
With the large-scale deployment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) mega-constellations (e.g., Starlink, OneWeb), traditional TCP exhibits severe performance bottlenecks over satellite links characterized by high latency, high dynamics, and high bit error rates.
The primary issue lies in the fact that standard TCP relies on packet loss as a congestion signal. Under hundreds-of-milliseconds round-trip times (RTTs) and frequent link disruptions, its slow start and retransmission mechanisms lead to significantly low throughput efficiency. 

To address these issues, an effective approach is to introduce a satellite-optimized TCP OAM. It will be a lightweight OAM capabilities to enhance transport robustness: 1. identify drop and congestion; 2. adaptive OAM packet rate; 3. compatible with existing TCP.

Let's discuss it on the side meeting.

bookings.title: Use Cases for Agentic AI Protocols
bookings.description: This IETF side meeting aims to discuss a concrete set of use cases and derive potential requirements for agentic AI protocols, with a primary focus on communication and collaboration between AI agents. While inter-agent interaction is central, the scope also includes related scenarios such as end users interacting with agents, agent-to-tool communication beyond traditional APIs, and the role of gateways. The agent lifecycle—such as discovery, onboarding, interaction, and evolution of agents—is considered in scope. The collected use cases will be used to evaluate existing and emerging protocols that fall within the IETF’s remit, assessing their suitability for specific scenarios and helping to identify gaps where new work or extensions may be needed.
